messages:
Maria G.: FYI Rack-14 is throwing intermittent ECC/Xid on 4 GPUs across two hosts since ~02:00 UTC. Not a full outage but elevated error/error-correcting rates :warning:
Kevin L.: Can you paste the failure snippets?
Maria G.: Sure — copied from host r14-n3: ``ERROR: GPU0 Xid=13 / ECC corrected=156 / ECC uncorrected=2`` and on r14-n7: ``ECC corrected=240 / Xid=31``
Sasha P.: Seen similar on rack 18 last month but that was a faulty riser. Symptoms here look like single-card flakiness though. Any thermal anomalies? :eyes:
Maria G.: Temps are nominal; GPUs 0 and 2 on r14-n3 hit 72C during batch, but fan curves normal. No power supply CS alarms.
Dmitri (hw): Xid 13 and 31 often map to memory parity/PCIe errors; could be bad card batch or subtle voltage sag under sustained kernel loads. How many reboots/drains?
Maria G.: We've drained two instances, did a soft reboot of n3 — GPU errors persist on pinned workloads. I pulled the CUDA driver log and saw repeated ECC reports during KV-cache heavy inference.
Kevin L.: Workload pattern: long context generations -> consistent KV growth. Could be exposing ECC threshold with continuous mem churn. Do we see any pattern in model size?
Maria G.: All affected jobs are >6B models, usually step 2048+ sequences during RLHF-ish evals.
Sasha P.: Suggest running memtest on suspect GPUs and swapping with a known-good card from rack 12. Also check riser and power cables on the host.
Dmitri (hw): Agreed. I'll schedule a hot-swap window. Meanwhile, infra-bot: mark hosts r14-n3,r14-n7 as degraded and block scheduling for GPU jobs.
infra-bot: action: set_degraded hosts=[r14-n3,r14-n7] reason="ECC/Xid spike" by=maria_g timestamp=1802501310
Ops Lead: Please capture core dumps and nv-hostengine logs before any full power cycle. We need data for RMA if hw flagged.
Maria G.: Collected `nvidia-smi -q` output and `dmesg | grep -i xid` to /tmp/r14-ecc-dump.tar.gz and uploaded to ops-case.
Kevin L.: Quick diag plan: 1) Swap GPU from rack12, 2) run stress mem test + 3x long-gen reproducer, 3) if reproduces, initiate RMA with serials.
Sasha P.: Also add a metric alert for ECC corrected rate per-card with a 10m window so we detect earlier. We only had infra-bot warnings at host-level.
Dmitri (hw): If swap clears errors, likely bad card(s). If swap follows errors to new card -> investigate host power/PCIe lanes.
Maria G.: Swapped GPU0 on n3 with spare from r12 at 03:45 UTC. Running reproducer now; will report.
infra-bot: alert: ECC_rate_high host=r14-n3 gpu=GPU0 value=184 window=5m threshold=50 (auto)
Kevin L.: Thanks. If swap fails, we should plan for full rack-level audit (connectors, backplane capacitance) before mass RMA.
Maria G.: Update at 04:12 UTC — reproducer still triggering Xid on swapped card, but at lower rate. Suspect intermittent connector contact.
Sasha P.: Schedule onsite for physical inspection during maintenance window. In the meantime, throttle long-context jobs off these nodes and route to other racks.
Ops Lead: Agreed. Throttled via scheduler policy `gpu.ecc.throttle` and added fallback routing to rack10/11.
Dmitri (hw): I'll pull serials and escalate to vendor with logs. If vendor says batch-related, we coordinate wider scan across racks for same batch IDs.
Maria G.: Putting short RCA notes: 1) Symptoms: ECC/Xid spikes on Rack-14 cards under sustained KV-cache load. 2) Immediate mitigation: drain/soft swap, throttle long-context jobs, degrade hosts. 3) Next actions: physical inspection, memtests, vendor RMA if card-level reproducible. 4) Instrumentation: per-card ECC alert, per-workload KV growth tagging.
Kevin L.: Add cost note: draining 2 hosts reduces available GPU capacity by ~8% for east region during peak. Ops, will patch schedulers to prefer dedicated spare pool for next 72h.
infra-bot: action: schedule_maintenance hosts=[r14-n3,r14-n7] window="2026-05-02T02:00:00Z" by=dmitri_hw
Maria G.: Thanks all — will post final RCA after vendor feedback. :thumbsup:
